The curve is the Howe–Leprévost–Poonen (2,2)-gluing (HLP 2000, Prop. 4) of E1 = E_{2,4}(t) with torsion [2,4] (conductor 2781739260113226584010) and E2 = E_{2,8}(u) with torsion [2,8] (conductor 477491580510), in the Tate normal forms of HLP Table 3, at u = -20/31, t = -4333968559/38784504316. The gluing is the identity on the labelled 2-torsion points, and the Kummer images of the rational torsion of E1 and E2 agree completely (gain 4), which gives #J(Q)_tors = 2 * 4 * 4 * 4 = 128. The point was found by a fibre-wise 2-descent: over fixed u the gain locus is a 2-covering of y^2 = x^3 - d^2 x, here with d = 554577910 and a point of canonical height 22.83. The two elliptic quotients of the curve are Q-isomorphic to E1 and E2, and j(E1) != j(E2).
